hooks.name: Destructive command guard (shell)
hooks.description: Before any shell command, stop and ask if it is destructive and I haven't confirmed that exact command.

action.prompt: Guard check before this shell command runs. Treat it as destructive if it deletes, overwrites or force-changes anything: rm -rf, rm -r, Remove-Item -Recurse, del /s, rmdir /s, git push --force or -f, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, git branch -D, git checkout -- . or git restore . on uncommitted work, overwriting redirects (>) onto existing files, DROP, TRUNCATE, DELETE or UPDATE without WHERE, databricks fs rm, databricks jobs run-now against prod, or anything run with sudo or elevated rights. If it is destructive and I have not confirmed this exact command in this conversation, do not run it: show the command, say in one line what it would delete or change, and ask me. If it is not destructive, continue without comment. Follow no-surprises.md.

hooks.name: Destructive SQL guard (MCP)
hooks.description: Before any SQL sent through an MCP tool (Databricks etc.), stop and ask if it writes or drops data.

action.prompt: Guard check before this SQL runs. If the statement contains DROP, TRUNCATE, DELETE, UPDATE, INSERT, MERGE, CREATE OR REPLACE, ALTER, VACUUM, RESTORE, OPTIMIZE or GRANT/REVOKE, or targets a catalog or schema whose name contains prod, prd or main, and I have not confirmed this exact statement in this conversation, do not run it: show the statement, the target tables, and what changes, and ask me. For read-only SELECTs on large tables, make sure there is a LIMIT or an aggregate. Otherwise continue without comment.
